scope: Finite sampled domain; no uniform bounds. Absolute shifts are in theta_E. Derivative scaled_error multiplies x/y/rho errors by rho and a1 errors by 1; photometric errors also divide by A. Exact contact derivatives excluded. Every timed call synchronizes; compilation separated, identical executable reused across small-transit, large-transit, and weak-wing regimes.
derivative_reference: Independent radial finite differences and central-slope extrapolation; source-centered complex-step integration in weak wings, refined from order64 to96
measurement_note: Runtime and NUTS used the explicitly configured 96/474 and 192/947 tables; later joint-table default changes do not alter these instances.

nuts.priors: q~Normal(0,2); rho/u0/theta_E exponential(.05q), flux exponential(.02q), a1=sigmoid(.25q), t0=.001q transit/.02q wings, baseline=truth+.001theta_E*q
nuts.scope: Two controlled synthetic scenarios and one noise realization each; fixed Einstein crossing time and orientation, no blend or proper motion. Same data and priors for every method. Report diagnostics and approximation errors with ESS/s.
nuts.timing_scope: Sampling includes compilation of the post-warmup sampling executable. Warmup+sampling totals include their compilation, but exclude solver construction, offline table building, initial truth-model evaluation, reference generation, and independent likelihood validation. These are not cold-process end-to-end timings.
nuts.posterior_comparison_scope: Posterior differences versus disk_64_32 use an independent-mean combined-MCSE heuristic. Methods use identical RNG seeds, so cross-method Monte Carlo covariance is unknown; these ratios are descriptive, not formal significance tests or numerical-bias bounds.
nuts.truth_astro_error_scope: truth_max_astro_error_sigma is Euclidean two-dimensional model error divided by nominal sigma_x. The independent likelihood checks and numerical_model_bias_mahalanobis_squared use the full anisotropic, correlated covariance.

reference_uncertainty.note: Independent-reference numerical refinement estimates, not rigorous error bounds; exact contact derivatives excluded
